_metadata.independence: Apart from the brief, I read only x20-re-input.json; no other repository file, web source or API was consulted.

hints.reason: AMAZON via the river's famous piranhas and PLANT via Mario's Piranha Plant; two unrelated worlds meet in one word with a real aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent cross-domain clue; facts accurate.

hints.reason: APPLE and TARGET via the William Tell legend, where the apple on his son's head is the target; a clean indirect aha.

pairs.pair_note: Strong indirect clue in the RELATIVE mould; lines accurate.

hints.reason: BAKERY via the Danish pastry and LEGO via its Danish origin; a crisp double meaning with a nice click.

pairs.pair_note: Lego was founded in Billund, Denmark; text accurate.

hints.reason: BARBIE via the famous 'shrimp on the barbie' line (barbie as barbecue, not the doll) and COCKTAIL via shrimp cocktail; misdirection off the doll makes it satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: The ad's actual words were roughly 'slip an extra shrimp on the barbie', but the text says the ad made the phrase famous, which is fair.

hints.reason: BASEBALL via the baseball diamond and SWEET via Neil Diamond's 'Sweet Caroline', with the Fenway singalong as a bonus tie.

pairs.pair_note: Clever layered clue; facts correct.

hints.reason: BEAR via Smokey Bear's 'Only you can prevent wildfires' and SMOKE because wildfires produce smoke (and the mascot is Smokey); fair and familiar.
hints.fix: Smokey Bear is the U.S. Forest Service's wildfire-prevention mascot, and wildfires pour out smoke.

pairs.pair_note: Explanation's 'named for smoke' is unsupported: Smokey was reportedly named after NYC fire chief 'Smokey' Joe Martin; use the fix.

hints.reason: FRANCE and BIKE both via the Tour de France bike race; easy but clean.

pairs.pair_note: Obvious, fair clue; 'about three weeks' is accurate.

hints.reason: BLOOD via blood plasma and TELEVISION via plasma TVs; a textbook double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Plasma is about 55% of blood volume; 'about half' is fine.

hints.reason: BOND via the SPECTRE organisation and 2015 film, GHOST via spectre meaning a ghost; the Bond spelling is familiar to U.S. players.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; text accurate.

hints.reason: BREAD because a baker bakes it and STREET via Sherlock Holmes's Baker Street; an instantly familiar phrase with a pleasant literary twist.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join that earns its place.

hints.reason: BRUSH via painter Bob Ross and FRIEND via Ross Geller of Friends; two huge pop-culture Rosses make a fun aha.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pop-culture clue.

hints.reason: BUTTERFLY via 'float like a butterfly, sting like a bee' and ROPE via the rope-a-dope; both are signature Ali references.

pairs.pair_note: Great clue; lines accurate.

hints.reason: CAR because you drive one and HARD via a computer hard drive; easy, clean double use.

pairs.pair_note: Simple but satisfying.

hints.reason: CHARGE via negative electric charge and PHOTO via film negatives; a neat science-and-film double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; text accurate.

hints.reason: CHESS via checkmate (mate is itself a chess term) and TEAM via teammate; familiar and quick.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but 'mate' stands alone in chess, which lifts it.

hints.reason: UMBRELLA via Mary Poppins's flying umbrella and CHIMNEY via Bert and the chimney sweeps of 'Step in Time'; iconic imagery on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; film details are accurate.

hints.reason: CLOSET via walk-in closet and SHOWER via walk-in shower; both instantly familiar home features, a tidy pairing.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join, but a satisfying matched set.

hints.reason: CODE via the Morse-code SOS and TITANIC via its famous distress calls; history and code meet neatly.

pairs.pair_note: The CQD mention is accurate and careful.

hints.reason: CONDUCTOR and TICKET via the classic image of a train conductor punching tickets; one scene but it holds both words.
hints.fix: Train conductors have traditionally punched tickets to mark them as used.

pairs.pair_note: Fair, slightly flat; 'often' is dated now that many tickets are scanned, hence the small fix.

hints.reason: COTTON and TAIL via the cottontail rabbit and its cotton-ball tail; easy and fair.
hints.fix: Cottontail rabbits are named for their white tails, which look like cotton balls.

pairs.pair_note: The COTTON line 'named for cotton' is loose; the fix states the actual link.

hints.reason: ROLL via the California roll and CRAB via its (imitation) crab filling; familiar food knowledge.

pairs.pair_note: Solid; ingredients line accurate.

hints.reason: CROW because crows build nests and SHIP via the crow's nest lookout; the literal and nautical senses click together.

pairs.pair_note: Nice; both senses supported.

hints.reason: DECK because jokers come in a standard deck and WILD via 'jokers wild'; clean card-game logic.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and fair.

hints.reason: DISNEY via Walt Disney World and SMALL via 'It's a Small World', the Disney ride, so the halves reinforce each other.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join with a thematic bonus (the ride is at Disney).

hints.reason: DRINK via fruit punch and LINE via punchline; quick and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Simple, familiar.

hints.reason: ENGINE via diesel engines and FAST via Vin Diesel in the Fast and Furious films; a fun pivot from machinery to movie star.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; car theme ties both sides.

hints.reason: FIELD via force field and STAR WARS via the Force; easy and familiar sci-fi pairing.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate.

hints.reason: FISHING via fishing bait and SWITCH via 'bait and switch'; the con is a metaphor from the fishing sense, which makes it click.

pairs.pair_note: Familiar phrase plus literal sense.

hints.reason: GENIE via Aladdin's magic lamp is strong, but SMOKE only connects through the genie-emerging-in-smoke image, so the second side leans on the first.

pairs.pair_note: Lamp alone does not suggest smoke; the smoke side exists only inside the genie scene. Text is accurate and appropriately hedged ('films often show').

hints.reason: HAT via the derby (bowler) hat and MINT via the Kentucky Derby's mint julep; indirect and satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Strong indirect clue; facts correct.

hints.reason: HOUSE because Gryffindor is a Hogwarts house and LION via its lion emblem; widely known.

pairs.pair_note: Fair pop-culture clue.

hints.reason: JOKE because a gag is a joke and ORDER via a gag order; the legal sense gives the second side a nice twist.

pairs.pair_note: Synonym on one side but an honest second connection.

hints.reason: LAUGH because sitcoms aim for laughs and TRACK via the sitcom laugh track; fair and quick.

pairs.pair_note: Track side depends on 'laugh track', but that phrase is very familiar.

hints.reason: MAP via an atlas as a book of maps and STRONG via the Titan Atlas holding up the sky; myth and reference book meet nicely.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; 'symbol of strength' is fair.

hints.reason: MERCURY because Hermes is his Greek counterpart and PURSE via the Hermes Birkin bag; a stylish aha, though some players will not know the brand.

pairs.pair_note: Brand is Hermès; the unaccented spelling is fine for play.

hints.reason: TOOTH via baby teeth and MILK because babies drink milk, with milk teeth tying the two together.

pairs.pair_note: Neat clue; 'milk teeth' is well enough known in the U.S.

hints.reason: NAIL via nail clippers and SHIP via the clipper sailing ship; a good double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate.

hints.reason: RAIN via the forty days of rain in Noah's flood and OLIVE via the dove's olive leaf; both are core story details.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate to Genesis.

hints.reason: PIN and TAIL both via Pin the Tail on the Donkey; an instantly familiar party game.
hints.fix: In Pin the Tail on the Donkey, blindfolded players try to pin a paper tail on a donkey picture.

pairs.pair_note: The PIN line never mentions the donkey; the fix links hint to target.

hints.reason: POTATO via potato chips and RAM via memory chips, with RAM misdirecting toward the animal; nice.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate.

hints.reason: SATURN via its rings and TRUNK via tree-trunk growth rings; a satisfying shared property.

pairs.pair_note: Lines nicely hedged ('often one per year').

hints.reason: TATTOO because ink is slang for a tattoo and SKIN because tattoo ink sits in the skin; fair and easy but flat.

pairs.pair_note: Low-delight pass; the skin side runs through the tattoo itself. Could be argued BORDERLINE as lazy.

hints.reason: STAR via Star Trek and TRIP because a trek is a long trip; easy but clean.

pairs.pair_note: Synonym on one side plus an iconic franchise.

hints.reason: WEB because spiders spin silk webs and WORM via silkworms spinning silk; a neat nature link.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate; lines avoid calling silkworms true worms.
